chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Uramah, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would pass by the graves of a group of believers, he would say: 'Peace be upon you from the dwellings of a believing people, and indeed we, if Allah wills, shall be joining you.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet (s.a.a.w.) say when passing by the graves of believers?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the Prophetic tradition of saluting the graves of believers, establishing a spiritual continuity between the living and the deceased. It underscores the Shia concept of *salat al-mayyit* (prayer for the dead) and the belief that the souls of the faithful remain aware of greetings from the living, reinforcing the communal bond of the *Ummah* across death. The phrase 'insha' Allah biha lahiqun' reflects the eschatological hope of resurrection and gathering in the Hereafter.
